newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Minister sees long-term decline in Portugal cereal.
newsitem.headline: Minister sees long-term decline in Portugal cereal.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Fernando Gomes da Silva was quoted as saying he believed cereals output would drop in Portugal in the coming years.

Asked if it was worthwhile to maintain the present level of cereals production amid strong competition from other European states, Gomes da Silva told Diario de Noticias newspaper, "No. It is evident that it is not worth it and that production will fall drastically in the coming years.

"Cereals are only justified in regions where there is good productivity because of natural conditions, as in the case of part of the Beja region (in southeast Portugal), or where it is possible to irrigate fields."
Gomes da Silva denied that Portugal was suffering from a drought.
"There is neither a general drought, nor generalised destruction of crops," he said.
He declined to estimate possible losses for farmers.
"We can only measure possible losses at the time of bringing in the harvest, in June and July," he said.
Rain levels have been low in Portugal this year, hitting cereals production.

Another senior government official, Deputy Secretary of State for Agriculture Carlos Cunha, said last month that a lack of rainfall had destroyed an estimated 50 to 70 percent of Portugal's winter cereal crops.
In 1996 Portugal, Europe's smallest cereals producer, harvested around 415,000 tonnes of wheat, up from 360,000 tonnes the previous year.
